items.title: Inside Jharkhand’s assembly gherao: Lathicharge, tear gas and conflicting claims
items.summary: Thousands of students from all districts of Jharkhand marched on the state assembly in Ranchi on Monday, demanding the cancellation of exams conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission over alleged paper leaks and irregularities. They also demanded a CBI probe into the allegations. Despite prohibitory orders under BNSS section 163 and heavy barricading with barbed wire, protesters broke through the security cordons and reached the assembly complex. The police responded with water cannons, tear gas and lathicharge, leaving several students injured. The police claimed that protesters pelted stones, injuring several security personnel. So, what really happened on the ground? Who used force, who resorted to violence, and how did the protest escalate? Watch. In times of misinformation, you need news you can trust. We’ve got you covered. Subscribe to Newslaundry and power our work. Why are students in Jharkhand angry? items.title: Supreme Court acquits man accused of raping minor; flags HC's failure to consider medical evidence
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday restored the acquittal of a man accused of raping a five-year-old girl [Ram Singh v. State of Himachal Pradesh] A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar set aside the Himachal Pradesh High Court judgment that had reversed the trial court's acquittal of Ram Singh. The apex court found that the High Court had failed to properly consider the medical and forensic evidence on record. “ We, therefore, find that the learned judge of the trial court had rightly acquitted the appellant (Ram Singh) of the said accusation. The High Court, in our view, failed to refer to the medical reports as well as the report of the forensic science laboratory (FSL) while overturning the acquittal of the appellant, ” the Court said. The Bench further added that the evidence on record created serious doubt about the prosecution case and was insufficient to establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt. “ The material in that regard falls short and it, in fact, creates a serious doubt about the version of the prosecution, ” the Court observed. items.title: TN Speaker’s anti-abortion rhetoric is more than a personal opinion
items.summary: Abortion rights in India are hard-won. In 2021, the Supreme Court observed in a landmark judgement that reproductive autonomy is a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution. That means a woman can choose whether or not to exercise her right to abortion. Gods of any religion and their earth-bound spokespersons have no say in women’s bodily autonomy. Yet accessing safe abortion, without judgement, remains a Herculean battle. Pro-life (anti-abortionist) noise continues to drown out the simple facts of choice and consent. Adding to that noise on August 9 were Catholic groups and Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker JCD Prabhakar who is also the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) MLA from Thousand Lights in Chennai. Speaking at an event organised by CHARIS India under the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of India (CBCI), Prabhakar declared: “Life begins at conception.” This has been the tiresome slogan of anti-abortionists globally. It is the regular rallying cry of Christian nationalist Republicans in the US who seek to wipe out reproductive rights under the guise of protecting ‘all life’.
